She has written six plays, and three of them were produced.

The yard gives them room for outdoor play.

senses.head: The place where something happened, especially a crime or an accident

examples: Please don't make a scene in front of the neighbors.

senses.head: A particular area of activity together with the people involved in it

senses.head: A main division of a play, or a short self-contained performance
examples: The first act runs almost an hour.
Most modern plays have two acts instead of five.

senses.head: A law passed by a legislature

Both acts cleared the Senate on the same day.

senses.head: Behavior that is put on to hide how someone really feels
examples: She seems confident, but it's an act.

entries.meaning: A play or film meant to be funny and to end happily. ---
examples: The theater is doing a comedy this spring.
He writes dark comedies about office life.

It would be a tragedy to lose the old theater.

senses.head: A serious play that ends unhappily for the main character
examples: Hamlet is the best known tragedy in English.
Greek tragedies were performed outdoors.
The director staged the tragedy in modern dress.

entries.meaning: A play in which the story is carried by songs and dancing. ---

entries.meaning: A stage performance that tells a story through formal dancing and music. ---

The two musical interludes are the best part of the evening.
The clowns come out during the interlude.

senses.head: A short period of time between two longer or busier ones
examples: The rain gave us a quiet interlude before the crowds arrived.
After a brief interlude in Texas, the family moved back east.
Those two years were a happy interlude in a hard decade.

senses.head: A short piece of music or performance between the main parts of a show
examples: A piano interlude covers the scene change.
The two musical interludes are the best part of the evening.
The clowns come out during the interlude.

entries.meaning: The imaginary wall between the actors and the audience. ---
examples: She breaks the fourth wall and asks the audience a question.
Most realistic plays keep the fourth wall firmly in place.
The narrator steps through the fourth wall in the first minute.

entries.meaning: A show made of songs, dances, and short comic scenes with no single story. ---
examples: The theater is doing a revue of songs from the thirties.
Small revues were once the standard summer program.
It is more of a revue than a play.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like review, the critic's article.

entries.meaning: An older American kind of variety show with singers, comics, and acrobats. ---
examples: His grandfather worked in vaudeville before the movies came in.
Vaudeville died out in the 1930s.
The whole number is a tribute to old vaudeville.
entries.contrast: Usually said in two syllables, VAWD-vil, with the middle e swallowed.

entries.meaning: A show of songs and comedy performed in a club while the audience sits at tables. ---
examples: She sings in a cabaret on the East Side.
The cabarets in that neighborhood stay open until three.
It is an intimate cabaret with about forty seats.
entries.contrast: The final t is silent and the stress falls on the last syllable: kab-uh-RAY.

entries.meaning: A line invented on the spot that is not in the script.
examples: That laugh line was an ad-lib on opening night.
Half his best ad-libs ended up in the final script.
The director hates an ad-lib of any kind.
